newsitem.title: USA: NYS Bruno plans to probe McCall for bids - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYS Bruno plans to probe McCall for bids - paper.

text.p: New York State Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, said he is ready to order a state Senate investigation of possible bid-rigging at the comptroller's office, the New York Post reported Monday.

Bruno also told the paper he might ask Gov George Pataki and state attonery general Dennis Vacco to investigate the decision by the comptroller to award a $44 million payroll computerization project to a single bidder, Anderson Consulting.
A total of 12 firms initially said they were interested in bidding on the contract, but only Anderson Counsulting, which helped design the project, turned in a bid.

The Senate Majority Leader made his comments days after Finance Committee staffers said they found what they called "smoking gun" letters sent to the state Comptroller H. Carl McCall last year, in which another nationally known computer firm complained about possible bid rigging, the paper said.
The contract involves rebuilding the state's computer system for issuing more than 200,000 paychecks every two weeks to all full- and part-time state workers.
McCall's spokesman told the paper last month that the comptroller's office had canvassed possible Anderson competitors to make sure there were no problems with the bidding process.
He could not be immediately reached for comment on Monday.
